video.title: From Golang To Odin: The Trade-offs You Need to Know

abstract: Anthony GG walks through moving his trading terminal Market Monkey from Go to Odin, showing what feels familiar, what gets faster or cleaner, and what new footguns appear. It matters because this is a real product-port discussion, not an abstract language war.
mainTakeaway: Odin gives him the low-level control, rendering path, and simplicity he wanted, but the trade-off is explicit memory management and more manual, less type-safe patterns than Go.

conclusion: His verdict is pragmatic: if you want a Go-like language with more direct control and strong performance for native UI work, Odin looks compelling. But you must be ready to own memory management, pointer safety, and interface-like abstractions yourself.
